text:
Now I want to love something far away…
some divine man
who is like a bird in his sweetness,
who has known countless women
and knows other lands, and whose word
blooms on his lips, perfumed:
like a virgin forest beneath the wind…


And I want to love him now. The afternoon is
soft and tranquil like thick moss,
my mouth trembles, and my fine fingers
slowly undo my braids.


I feel a vague murmur… All the earth
is singing sweetly… Far away,
the forests have filled with corollas,
the streams overflow their beds
and the waters seep into the earth
as my eyes seep into the eyes
I dream of, enraptured…


But…
the sun is already sinking behind the mountains,
the birds huddle in their nests,
the afternoon must die and he is far away…
far away like this sun that forever
departs and leaves me, with my hands
buried in my braids, my mouth
moist and trembling, my soul
made subtle, afire with hope
of this infinite love that makes me
sweet and beautiful…

translation.title: This Afternoon
translation.editorial_note: The translation preserves the speaker's sensuous, dreamlike progression from the late afternoon landscape to the absent beloved and keeps the short “But…” turn as a hinge.
